correctness.rationale: The b+1 ordered gaps of ones give a bijection with weak compositions of a into b+1 parts, including both endpoint gaps. Fixing one or two distinct gaps gives the two binomial probability ratios in the proof. Counts at distinct lengths have no same-gap cross term. For x_b=a/b and u=r+s, the first-order relative coefficient of p_j about g_j(x_b) is -j(j-1)/(2x_b)+j(j+1)/(2(1+x_b)); the coefficient of p_{r,s} about g_r g_s is -1-u(u-1)/(2x_b)+(u+2)(u+1)/(2(1+x_b)). Accounting for (b+1)b versus (b+1)^2 yields -2-rs/x_b+(rs+r+s+1)/(1+x_b), the stated kernel after putting over a common denominator. Fixed lengths and x_b bounded away from zero and infinity control the remainder. The upward quadratic has two positive roots iff its discriminant is strictly positive, since its sum and product of roots are positive. At total length u<=9 the bound rs>=u-1 excludes the positive phase; at u=10 the discriminant is positive only at (1,9). For those lengths the ratio of the mixed moment to the product of the means has positive denominator (b+1)a(n-10)(n-11) on the claimed domain. Subtraction gives the polynomial F, whose three specializations are -4t(t^2+3t+32), t(t+13)(3t-19), and -5t(5t^2-54t+97). The last bracket is positive at t=10 and increasing thereafter, and the other signs are strict.
